prompt.context: Our client is a major US media and entertainment company that has over 50 years of experience in making Hollywood. While its movies continue to dominate Setflix charts, TV series have been gaining in market share.
prompt.question: The client has hired you to advise if they should invest in creating a Setflix focused division for series programming or chill, and if so — which category should they target first?

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's return target?
What part of the value chain is the client considering?
clarifying_info.a: End to end: Creation/Ideation, Production, and Distribution

clarifying_info.q: Which customer segments should we consider?

exhibits.title: Setflix User Demographics and Payout Rates by Genre
exhibits.shows: A two-part table. The top section shows the number of Setflix users (millions) by age demographic and their percentage conversion rates for Horror, Comedy, and Action categories. The bottom section shows per-view payout rates (in dollars) for each category based on three view-count tiers.

framework: Market: size of the Setflix TV series opportunity, genre-level demand, competitive landscape
Financials: expected revenue by genre (views × payout), one-time and recurring production costs, ROI / NPV
Strategic fit: client's existing competencies in content creation, management buy-in, risk of brand dilution or cannibalization

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate total expected views and revenue for Comedy and Action genres. Which genre should the client prioritize?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note Horror is visibly lower in conversion across most demographics and skip detailed calculation. For Comedy and Action, multiply users by conversion rate per demographic, sum to get total views, then apply the appropriate payout tier. Action edges out Comedy on revenue.

math.setup: Total Views = sum over demographics of (# Setflix users × % conversion). Payout tier is determined by whether total views fall below 40M, between 40–60M, or above 60M.
steps: Comedy views — 1-16: 30M×0.35=10.5M; 16-30: 50M×0.35=17.5M; 30-60: 60M×0.40=24M; 60+: 18M×0.50=9M; Total=61M (rounds reported as 62.1M in casebook)
Action ($9.48M) > Comedy ($8.68M) — Action is the higher-revenue genre
math.answer: Action genre expected annual revenue ≈ $9.48M; Comedy ≈ $8.68M. Action is preferred.

questions.prompt: Calculate the one-time production costs and annual recurring costs for launching an Action TV series.
questions.guidance: Candidate should categorize costs into one-time (writing/ideation, production, casting) and annual recurring (marketing, SG&A), then sum each bucket.

math.setup: One-time costs: Writing/Ideation + Production + Casting. Annual costs: Marketing + SG&A.

questions.prompt: Using a 20% discount rate, calculate the NPV of entering the Action TV series market. Does it meet the 14% ROI hurdle?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the perpetuity NPV formula: NPV = –One-Time Investment + (Annual Profit / Discount Rate). Annual profit = revenue minus annual costs. A positive NPV substantially above zero and an implied return well above 14% confirms the investment.

math.setup: NPV = –One-Time Investment + (Annual Revenue – Annual Cost) / Discount Rate
math.answer: NPV ≈ $26M, well above zero and comfortably exceeding the 14% ROI hurdle.

brainstorming.prompt: What are all the levers the client should consider when deciding whether to enter the Setflix TV series market?

categories.name: Market
ideas: Size of the Setflix TV series market globally
Competitive intensity — other Hollywood studios already on Setflix
Barriers to entry for each genre
Audience demographic trends and streaming habits

categories.name: Financials
ideas: Risk of show underperforming viewership targets

categories.name: Strategic
ideas: Client's existing creative competencies in film vs. series format
Management buy-in and organizational change required
Brand dilution risk — mixing TV series with premium film brand
Cannibalization of existing movie revenue on Setflix
Potential for franchise extensions across movies and series
Partnership or acquisition vs. build-from-scratch options

recommendation: The client should create a Setflix-focused TV series division; the NPV of future cash flows is approximately $26M, exceeding the 14% ROI target.
The division should launch with an Action series, which is projected to generate the highest annual revenue at ~$9.48M across all demographics.
risks: Opportunity cost — capital and management attention diverted from core film business
Cannibalization of existing movie viewership on Setflix
Lack of in-house competency in episodic TV series production and storytelling
next_steps: Hire or contract experienced script writers and showrunners for an action TV series
Secure management buy-in and allocate budget for the new division
Develop a detailed production timeline and pilot episode plan
